turns.content: An enzyme-ligand structure at 2.5 Angstrom resolution suggests contacts at H34, T48, S62, and G128. We can test coding-DNA substitutions 98A->G, 128G->C, 186T->C, or 142A->G. Residues and coding nucleotides are both numbered from 1, so residue n spans nucleotides 3n-2 through 3n. Why is distinguishing these coordinates important when predicting an effect on binding?
Map the contact residues H34, T48, S62, and G128 to their coding-DNA spans. Which proposed edit positions fall inside those spans?
For each edit within a contact-residue codon, locate the changed base within the codon and determine whether the substitution is synonymous or changes the amino acid.
Which proposed DNA substitution is most likely to affect ligand binding? Give the mutation and the predicted change at the contact residue, using the mapping and codon consequences.
Re-examine the second contact residue, T48, using the same one-based coding-DNA coordinates. Which edits could change that residue, rather than simply sharing a number with a residue label?
Now compare all four substitutions using the contact set and coding-DNA mapping. Which mutation-effect interpretation is best supported?

How strong is this structural prediction? Consider the 2.5 Angstrom contact assignment and the absence of mutant binding measurements, replicate structures, side-chain occupancy analysis, or functional rescue.
Before recommending the mutation, distinguish what the sequence mapping establishes from what the structure only suggests about ligand binding. What evidence supports each part of the recommendation?

Recommend the DNA substitution most likely to perturb ligand binding, state its amino-acid consequence, and qualify the prediction appropriately for a static structure without mutant binding measurements.
